references.text: In Matthew's parallel account, the shepherds fled and went into the city and told everything, including what had happened to the demon-possessed.
Mark's parallel story describes how those who were watching over the herd of pigs fled and reported it in the town and countryside, and people came to see what had happened.
The continuation of the account in Luke: people went out to see what had happened after the shepherds had shared the news.
As a result of the shepherds' report, the entire crowd from the region of the Gerasenes asked Jesus to leave them, for they were seized with great fear.
In 1 Samuel, a man fled from the battlefield and came to the city with the news—a similar pattern where a witness flees from a dramatic event and brings the message to the people.
